title: What did people use before refrigerators?
sources: Smithsonian Institution History of Home Refrigeration
American Society of Heating, Refrigerating Engineers

lines.text: Before electric refrigerators were invented in the nineteen-twenties, how did families keep their milk and meat from spoiling?
lines.caps: How did people keep *food cold | before *refrigerators?

lines.text: Every household relied on a wooden cabinet lined with tin or zinc, called an icebox.
lines.caps: Every kitchen relied on a *wooden | insulated *icebox

lines.text: During freezing winters, commercial ice harvesters sawed millions of tons of natural ice blocks from frozen northern lakes.
lines.caps: Harvesters sawed *giant ice blocks | from frozen northern *lakes!

lines.text: The giant blocks were packed in sawdust insulation and stored in massive icehouses until hot summer months.
lines.caps: Packed in sawdust to *keep ice frozen | all through the *summer

lines.text: Every week, the local iceman delivered twenty-five pound ice blocks with iron tongs straight into home kitchens.
lines.caps: The iceman carried *25-pound blocks | straight into your *kitchen!

lines.text: Families placed the melting ice in the top compartment, allowing dense cold air to sink over meat and butter.
lines.caps: Cold air sank *naturally | over butter, milk, and *meat

lines.text: Electric refrigeration transformed global nutrition, food safety, and modern civilization forever.
lines.caps: Electric cooling changed *food safety | and human health *forever!
